programs.name: Epic MegaGrants
programs.amount: Varies by project; awards have started around $5,000
programs.funds: Projects built with Unreal Engine, plus open-source 3D graphics tools and education.
programs.eligibility: Individuals, teams and companies anywhere that use Unreal Engine or contribute to the open-source 3D ecosystem.
programs.window: Two cycles a year. 2026: Cycle 1 ran Jan 12 to Mar 20 (notices Jun 15 to 19); Cycle 2 ran Jun 29 to Sep 4 (notices Dec 7 to 11).

programs.name: Unity for Humanity Grant
programs.amount: $600,000 pool shared by about ten winners (2026)
programs.funds: Real-time 3D projects tackling social and environmental issues aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
programs.eligibility: Creators worldwide building with Unity.
programs.window: Annual call. The 2026 call closed Feb 20, 2026 and winners have been announced.

programs.name: UK Games Fund: Content Fund
programs.funds: Equity-free grants for commercial games-for-entertainment content.
programs.eligibility: UK-based studios.
programs.window: Expressions of interest open.

programs.name: UK Games Fund: Prototype and Starter funds
programs.amount: Varies by round
programs.funds: Equity-free support for early prototypes and first projects. Prototype rounds have run regularly since 2015.
programs.eligibility: UK-based developers and new studios.
programs.window: Periodic rounds; check the fund's site for the current round.

programs.name: Video Games Expenditure Credit (VGEC)
programs.amount: 34% credit on qualifying core expenditure (applied to up to 80% of core costs)
programs.funds: Design, production and testing costs of games intended for public release.
programs.eligibility: UK companies whose game is certified British by the BFI, with at least 10% of core costs relating to UK activity.
programs.window: Claimed through the corporation tax return. Games starting from Apr 1, 2025 must use VGEC; the old relief (VGTR) closes Apr 1, 2027.

programs.name: Creative Europe MEDIA: Video Games and Immersive Content Development
programs.amount: Lump sum up to €200,000, covering up to 60% of eligible costs (2026 call)
programs.funds: Development of narrative video games and immersive content with international potential.
programs.eligibility: Companies established in countries taking part in Creative Europe MEDIA. From 2026, one application per coordinator.
programs.window: Annual call. The 2026 deadline was Feb 11, 2026; the next call usually opens late in the year with an early-year deadline.

programs.name: Digital Games Tax Credit (Section 481A)
programs.amount: 32% of eligible expenditure, up to €25 million per game
programs.funds: Design, production and testing of games. Extended in 2026 to post-release content for up to three years.
programs.eligibility: Irish-resident companies, or EEA companies trading in Ireland through a branch, with qualifying spend of at least €100,000 and a cultural certificate.
programs.window: Ongoing; requires a cultural certificate from the Minister.

programs.name: Video Game Tax Credit (CIJV)
programs.org: CNC and the French tax administration
programs.amount: 30% of eligible creation costs, capped at €6 million per company per year
programs.funds: Creation and development expenses for approved games. Available for expenses incurred until Dec 31, 2031.
programs.eligibility: Companies subject to French corporation tax, with a development budget of at least €100,000 and CNC approval.
programs.window: Ongoing; starts with provisional approval from the CNC.

programs.name: Video Game Aid Fund (FAJV)
programs.amount: Selective grants from writing support up to production support, capped at 50% of costs
programs.funds: Writing, pre-production and production of games produced in France.
programs.eligibility: Studios established in France.
programs.window: Several committee sessions a year (2026 sessions included March 30 and June 29).

programs.name: Federal Games Funding (Games-Förderung des Bundes)
programs.org: Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR), managed by DLR
programs.amount: Projects from €300,000; up to €8 million per project
programs.funds: Prototypes and production of games, including personnel, licenses, testing, community management, marketing and trade fairs.
programs.eligibility: Games companies in Germany. A draft consultation with the DLR project manager comes before the application.
programs.window: Open call since Aug 1, 2025, with about €125 million available in 2026.

programs.name: Game development and launch funding
programs.amount: Development up to NOK 2 million; launch and marketing up to NOK 1 million
programs.funds: Development, launch and marketing of Norwegian games.
programs.eligibility: Norwegian game companies.
programs.window: Funding rounds through the year. The first 2026 round awarded NOK 18.6 million to 12 projects.

programs.name: Games Scheme (Spilordningen)
programs.amount: Varies by project
programs.funds: Concept development, project development and production of Danish games.
programs.eligibility: Danish game developers.
programs.window: Application rounds through the year.

programs.name: Prototyping Program
programs.amount: Spring 2026 round: 22 projects shared $4.8 million
programs.funds: Early-stage builds that demonstrate a product's intended functionality and design.
programs.eligibility: Canadian-owned and controlled companies; see the CMF guidelines.
programs.window: Final closing date: Nov 10, 2026.

programs.name: Innovation and Experimentation Program
programs.amount: Spring 2026 round: 10 projects shared $9.2 million
programs.funds: Production of innovative interactive projects, including games, beyond the prototype stage.
programs.eligibility: Canadian-owned and controlled companies; see the CMF guidelines.
programs.window: Two windows in 2026 (Apr 10 to 21 and Aug 25 to Sep 15), both closed.

programs.name: Video Games Business Development Program
programs.org: Canada Media Fund and Creative BC
programs.amount: The second cohort shared $1 million (March 2026)
programs.funds: Business development for British Columbia video game studios.
programs.eligibility: Studios based in British Columbia.
programs.window: 2026 window ran Aug 21 to Sep 28 (closed).

programs.name: Interactive Digital Media Fund
programs.amount: Concept Definition: up to 50% of Ontario costs, max C$50,000. Production: up to 50%, max C$300,000.
programs.funds: Concept definition and production of interactive digital media, including games.
programs.eligibility: Ontario-based interactive digital media companies.
programs.window: Set intake deadlines each year; check Ontario Creates.

programs.name: Ontario Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (OIDMTC)
programs.amount: Up to 40% of eligible Ontario expenditures
programs.funds: Development of interactive digital media products, including games.
programs.eligibility: Ontario corporations that develop eligible products.
programs.window: Claimed after certification by Ontario Creates.

programs.name: Tax Credit for the Production of Multimedia Titles
programs.amount: Up to 37.5% of eligible labour (32.5% refundable plus 5% non-refundable, tax years beginning in 2026)
programs.funds: Labour costs of producing multimedia titles, including video games.
programs.eligibility: Qualified Quebec corporations certified by Investissement Québec.
programs.window: Claimed annually with the corporate tax return.

programs.name: Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit
programs.amount: 25% refundable credit on eligible B.C. salaries and wages (wages after Aug 31, 2025)
programs.funds: Labour for developing interactive digital media products, including games.
programs.eligibility: Corporations with a permanent establishment in British Columbia.
programs.window: Permanent; claimed annually.

programs.name: Digital Games Tax Offset (DGTO)
programs.org: Australian Taxation Office and the Office for the Arts
programs.amount: 30% refundable offset; minimum A$500,000 qualifying spend; cap A$20 million a year
programs.funds: New games, porting to new platforms, and ongoing development of released games.
programs.eligibility: Australian companies, or foreign companies with an Australian permanent establishment, with an ABN and a certificate from the Minister for the Arts.
programs.window: Ongoing; completion, porting or ongoing-development certificates.

programs.name: Game Development Sector Rebate (GDSR)
programs.amount: 20% of eligible NZ expenditure; minimum NZ$250,000 a year; cap NZ$3 million a year per studio
programs.funds: Game development expenditure incurred in New Zealand.
programs.eligibility: NZ-resident businesses, or foreign businesses with an NZ permanent establishment, that have an NZ company number.
programs.window: Annual. 2026: registration Jan 20 to Feb 27, applications Apr 1 to May 15.

programs.name: Texas Moving Image Industry Incentive Program
programs.amount: Cash grant of 5% ($100,000 to $1M Texas spend), 10% ($1M to $1.5M) or 25% ($1.5M and up), plus 1% to 2.5% uplifts
programs.funds: Texas wages and in-state spending on games for PC, console, mobile, browser, handheld and arcade.
programs.eligibility: At least 35% of paid employees and contractors are Texas residents and at least 60% of production happens in Texas.
programs.window: Applications accepted on a rolling basis; check the commission's guidelines.
